newsitem.title: USA: Fremont sees deal adding to 1998 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Fremont sees deal adding to 1998 earnings.

text.p: Fremont General Corp chief financial officer Wayne Bailey said he expects the acquisition of Industrial Indemnity Holdings Inc to contribute substantially to 1998 earnings.
Bailey, speaking to Reuters in a telephone interview, said he was comfortable with analysts' 1998 earnings estimate of $3.65-$3.75 a share, compared with previous estimates of about $3.30 a share.
He also said he was comfortable with analysts' 1999 estimates of $4.10-$4.25 a share.

Fremont earlier announced it had agreed to acquire Industrial Indemnity from Xerox Corp's Talegen Holdings Inc subsidiary for $365 million in cash and the payment of a $75 million debt obligation Industrial Indemnity has to Talegen.

Fremont expects part of the contribution to earnings to come from a sharp increase in investment income and from some cost savings through the consolidation of the companies' California operations, Bailey said.
He said he expects 1998 cost savings in a range of $20-$25 million.
Industrial Indemnity also will bring Fremont invested assets of about $1.2 billion, which analysts said could generate an additional $84 million in investment income.
Bailey said he estimates consolidated investment income from the insurance operations at $185 million in 1998.
The deal is expected to close late in the third quarter or early in the fourth quarter of 1997.
Fremont shares rose 2-3/8, or more than eight percent, to 31.
Bailey said the acquisition will give Fremont, the largest monoline writer of workers compensation insurance, welcome diversification outside of its strongholds in California and the midwest.

"I think Industrial Indemnity has a tremendous reputation in the marketplace and what it brought to us is not only some premium in California, where we have some expense savings, but also in the surrounding states," Bailey said.
"They were large in Utah, Texas, Idaho, Arizona, Hawaii, Oregon and Alaska and so it brought us some real geographic diversification to our premium base," he said.
